title: Joe Biden says he felt ‘as if there were two Donald Trumps’ after the head of the Republican Party privately shared ‘very generous’ words of wisdom when the Democrat took over the presidency in 2020
content:
Former President Joe Biden says a private letter Donald Trump left for him in the Oval Office in 2021 revealed a strikingly different side to him.

In his memoir Promise Me, America, Biden describes it as though there were “two Donald Trumps,” contrasting Trump’s private message with his public actions surrounding the disputed 2020 election and the January 6 attack on the Capitol.

The letter’s contents were first reported by The New York Times. Biden’s memoir is scheduled for publication November 17.

What Trump wrote to Biden

Trump left the letter for Biden on January 20, 2021, the day Biden was inaugurated as the 46th president. He addressed it simply to “46.”

Trump praised Biden’s love for America and his potential as a leader. He told Biden that he now had the opportunity to choose the place he would occupy in history and expressed confidence that Biden would remain true to himself and the American people.

The letter contained no attacks on Biden and did not dispute the election results.

Trump was 74 at the time, while Biden was 78.

Biden was surprised by the tone

Biden writes that Trump’s private message contrasted sharply with his refusal to participate in traditional presidential transition rituals.

He described one Trump as refusing the customary gestures toward his successor, while another appeared to wish him well warmly, “as an old friend would.”

After the inauguration, Biden showed the letter to several aides but did not allow them to read it. He described its contents only as “very generous.”

A letter written after a bitter transition

The warmth of the message stood in stark contrast to the circumstances surrounding Biden’s inauguration.

The Electoral College formally certified Biden’s victory in December 2020, but Trump refused to concede. He also skipped Biden’s inauguration and broke other presidential traditions, including hosting the incoming president and first lady for tea at the White House.

The transition followed weeks of false claims about election fraud and escalating efforts to challenge Biden’s victory.

Biden’s memoir condemns Trump over January 6

Elsewhere in the memoir, Biden offers a far harsher assessment of Trump’s role in the January 6 attack.

Biden wrote that Trump “led an insurrection” in an effort to remain in power after voters had rejected him.

Biden wrote that Trump’s actions on January 6, 2021 should never be forgotten and should follow him to his grave.

He also criticized Trump’s decision to grant broad pardons and clemency to defendants charged in connection with the Capitol attack after returning to office. Biden faulted Trump for failing to hold a formal ceremony honoring the police officers who defended the Capitol.

The contrast between those accusations and Trump’s private letter is central to Biden’s description of the former president.

Trump and Biden had another friendly encounter

Biden describes another unexpected display of warmth during a 2024 Oval Office meeting after Trump defeated Vice President Kamala Harris in the presidential election.

The two met on November 13, 2024, and it lasted nearly two hours.

Biden writes that Trump’s demeanor was so friendly that he initially wondered whether Trump was putting him on.

According to the memoir, Trump told Biden that if politics were removed from the equation, the two could be good friends.

Biden says he was too stunned to respond.

Trump also praised Biden’s record on job creation as “extraordinary” and said he was relieved he had not been forced to run against Biden, according to the memoir.

White House attacks Biden

White House communications director Steven Cheung did not dispute the authenticity of the letter when asked about it and the memoir.

Instead, Cheung argued that Biden should have followed the advice Trump offered in the letter.

He accused Biden of having “tried to destroy this country” and of weaponizing the justice system against political opponents. Cheung also called Biden “a disgrace.”

The response highlights the continuing political divide between the two presidents despite Biden’s account of their private interactions.

Biden addresses his health

Biden also addressed his health and the memoir’s rollout in a social media post on November 8.

He said his doctors “continue to be encouraged” by his response to treatment, while acknowledging that some days are better than others and that treatment can sometimes slow him down.

Biden said he would not be able to participate in as many conversations about the book as he had hoped but expressed confidence that the memoir would speak for itself.

The Associated Press describes Biden as 83 and Trump as 80.

Biden’s account ultimately presents a complicated picture of Trump, separating the private warmth he encountered in two Oval Office interactions from the public conduct he says defined Trump’s presidency and post-election actions.

title: U.K. police arrest U.S. Army soldier on suspicion of espionage on behalf of Russia, FBI Director Kash Patel says the allegations are ‘of the utmost concern’
content:
British counterterrorism police arrested a 41-year-old U.S. Army soldier near Gloucester, England , on suspicion of espionage on behalf of Russia.

FBI Director Kash Patel said the allegations were “of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies,” according to a Metropolitan Police news release.

The soldier has not been charged and authorities have not identified him or disclosed his rank.

Patel warns against breaking the oath

The FBI director said the bureau “has no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States” and puts American national security or that of its allies at risk.

He added that the investigation remained ongoing.

What police say happened

The Metropolitan Police said the soldier was arrested on suspicion of violating two sections of the National Security Act 2023.

The alleged offenses involve obtaining or disclosing protected information and assisting a foreign intelligence service.

A police statement cited by ABC News said “the country to which the allegations relate is Russia.”

The soldier was arrested near Gloucester and remained at a London police station as of about 6:45 p.m. local time, according to police.

Officers also searched two locations in Gloucestershire.

The Metropolitan Police said the case was not connected to any other counterterrorism investigation. Counter Terrorism Policing London is leading the investigation with assistance from U.S. authorities, the U.S. military and the FBI.

Police have not released the soldier’s name or rank. IBTimes UK reported that he had not been charged.

Army calls suspect a “senior soldier”

Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, commanding general of the U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command, described the suspect as a “senior soldier, entrusted with sensitive information.”

Stinchon called the alleged conduct a “sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent.”

He urged anyone who notices suspicious activity to report it to a local counterintelligence office.

Vicki Evans, a deputy assistant commissioner and senior national coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing, also described the allegations as serious.

“Our investigation is very much ongoing,” she said.

Evans said the operation demonstrated the strength of UK-U.S. law enforcement and national security cooperation and praised the teams involved in the investigation.

Soldier reportedly served with NATO

The Associated Press reported that the soldier was serving with NATO’s Allied Rapid Reaction Corps at Imjin Barracks near Gloucester.

The report cited a U.S. official, a senior NATO official and a British government official who spoke anonymously because they were discussing sensitive military matters.

The U.S. official told The Associated Press that the soldier is an officer.

The BBC also reported that he was posted to Imjin Barracks in Innsworth.

However, IBTimes UK noted that the Metropolitan Police have not confirmed the posting.

Authorities have not disclosed the soldier’s specific duties, whether he had access to classified information or what conduct led to the espionage allegations.

Arrest comes amid concern over Russian activity

The arrest comes as the U.S. and European governments face growing concerns about Russian espionage and other covert activity.

The Associated Press reported that several European countries have recently warned about alleged Russian operations involving sabotage, espionage and drone incursions.

The developments have contributed to heightened security concerns surrounding American military personnel and facilities in Britain.

The investigation into the soldier remains ongoing and authorities have not publicly detailed what information he allegedly obtained or disclosed, or what assistance he is suspected of providing to Russian intelligence.

title: Robert F. Kennedy’s children fight to shut down President Donald Trump’s 250-foot triumphal arch near Arlington National Cemetery, call it a ‘permanent denigration’ of the late senator’s gravesite
content:
Members of the Kennedy family are asking a federal court to block President Donald Trump‘s planned 250-foot arch near Arlington National Cemetery, arguing that the structure would permanently damage the gravesites of their relatives and the views surrounding them.

Nine Kennedy family members filed a motion on November 10 in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia seeking to join an existing lawsuit and asking the court to declare the project unlawful and halt construction through preliminary and permanent injunctions.

The relatives argued that the arch would cast shadows over the graves of President John F. Kennedy, Senator Robert F. Kennedy and other family members while obstructing a view that President Kennedy cherished.

The filing said the structure “constitutes nothing less than a permanent denigration of the Kennedy Gravesites and the final resting place for Plaintiffs’ parents and grandparents.”

Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Trump’s secretary of Health and Human Services, did not join the lawsuit.

White House defends the project

White House spokesman Davis Ingle told Newsweek on November 10 that an “activist district court” had temporarily blocked the project.

Ingle criticized the participation of Kennedy family members in the lawsuit and said the judiciary should not be used to politicize a structure the administration says is intended to unite the country.

The White House said it remained confident it would prevail as the case moves forward.

Trump has described the proposed structure as “the greatest and most beautiful triumphal arch, anywhere in the world.”

Which Kennedy family members sued?

The nine plaintiffs are children and grandchildren of Robert and Edward M. Kennedy.

Rory Kennedy and Maxwell Kennedy said in a statement that Americans from across the country visit Arlington to honor those who served and sacrificed.

Attorneys Norman Eisen and Steve Jonas described the proposed arch as an illegal interference with Arlington National Cemetery and the people commemorated there, including the gravesites of the Kennedy brothers and Ethel Kennedy.

The family members are seeking to intervene in a broader lawsuit brought by Washington, D.C. and Virginia against the Trump administration. Several Vietnam War veterans are also challenging the project.

The underlying dispute centers on whether the arch qualifies as a commemorative work under the Commemorative Works Act of 1986, which requires congressional authorization for certain memorial projects.

Kennedys argue arch would damage cemetery views

The family’s filing says the project would cause “irrevocable adverse impacts” to the area, including the Kennedy gravesites and views between Arlington National Cemetery and the National Mall.

The lawsuit argues that the 250-foot structure would be more than twice the height of the Lincoln Memorial and would dwarf other national monuments.

The Kennedys also pointed to the location of President Kennedy’s grave.

His gravesite was placed along a direct line from Arlington House across Memorial Bridge toward the Lincoln Memorial. The filing quotes Kennedy as saying of the view: “I could stay here forever.”

The family members said they often visit the gravesites early in the morning to avoid crowds and look toward the view, writing that they are “comforted by the fact that their fathers and uncles loved that view.”

Dave Aronberg, a former Palm Beach County state attorney, told Newsweek on November 10 that a federal injunction is the mechanism available to immediately halt administrative action.

He said a court cannot erase an agency’s internal vote but can make its decision legally unenforceable while the court considers the case or Congress intervenes.

Planning commission approved the arch

The National Capital Planning Commission approved the project in an 8-4 vote following a 9½-hour hearing that included testimony from numerous opponents.

U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan then issued a 14-day temporary restraining order on November 5, less than two hours after the commission’s vote.

The order prohibits construction, excavation, demolition and road closures at or around Memorial Circle, the traffic island between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.

In a 33-page opinion, Chutkan found that the challengers were likely to establish that the project violates the Commemorative Works Act.

“Congress has not enacted any statute authorizing construction of the Arch,” Chutkan wrote.

The commission’s vote also reflected a political divide. Members who supported the project were connected to the Trump administration or the president, while opponents represented Washington, D.C.

Commissioner Paul Ingrassia, a General Services Administration lawyer, said the arch was “not about politics” but about remembrance.

What happens next?

Chutkan’s temporary restraining order is set to expire after 14 days unless she extends it while considering a longer injunction, putting the current deadline around November 19.

The judge also ordered the government to submit a status report demonstrating compliance with the order.

The White House defended the project after the ruling, posting on X that the arch would “honor the heroes who gave everything for our nation.”

The Kennedy family’s intervention adds another prominent group of opponents to a legal battle already involving the District of Columbia, Virginia and Vietnam War veterans.

The court must now decide whether to extend the restrictions and ultimately whether the Trump administration can proceed with construction of the arch.

title: ‘We can’t normalize behavior like this’: Ohio Governor-elect Amy Acton says she has ‘no intention’ of speaking with former rival Vivek Ramaswamy due to his ‘despicable’ campaign ad featuring her estranged mother
content:
Ohio Gov.-elect Amy Acton, a Democrat, said she has “no intention” of speaking with Republican Vivek Ramaswamy after defeating him in the November 3 gubernatorial election.

Acton also condemned a campaign advertisement featuring her estranged mother, calling the spot “terrible and despicable.”

Acton made the comments November 6 during her first television interview since the election on CBS Mornings. Asked whether she had spoken with Ramaswamy after the race, Acton said she had not.

“I think we can’t normalize behavior like this. It was so beyond the pale, so no, I have no intention of speaking to him,” Acton said. “I do believe that leaders’ words matter, and we need to hold folks accountable.”

Acton attacks campaign ad

Ohio Governor-elect Amy Acton said she has no intention of speaking to Vivek Ramaswamy after defeating him on Nov. 3. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM/MEGA

Acton said she believed the Ramaswamy campaign turned to the advertisement because it was struggling in the final stages of the race.

“I think he did it because they were struggling in their campaign. There was polling that had come out. They were six to seven points behind,” Acton said.

She said the ad was not merely unexpected but part of a broader campaign strategy she considered unacceptable.

“There was no low” Ramaswamy would not “sink to,” she said, adding that she believed Ohio voters “see through that.”

Ramaswamy’s concession call

Vivek Ramaswamy said he called Amy Acton to concede the gubernatorial race but reached voicemail. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM/MEGA

On election night, Ramaswamy said he called Acton to concede but reached her voicemail.

“I left her a message,” he said in his concession speech.

Acton’s comments to CBS Mornings suggest the two have not spoken since the election.

Ramaswamy described the contest as a “tough race” that was “bitter at times in both directions.”

“I wish her well to lead this state to hopefully greater heights in the future,” he said.

The ad featuring Acton’s mother

The political advertisement challenged Amy Acton’s childhood account of living in a tent and questioned her truthfulness. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM / MEGA

The 60-second advertisement featured Acton’s estranged mother, Donna Arthur, speaking directly to Ohio voters and urging them not to elect her daughter.

“I love my daughter, but when I saw her lying about her opponent—and it’s not easy for a mother to say this—but Amy has a serious problem,” Arthur says in the video. “She is a liar. She lies about her past.”

The advertisement also challenged Acton’s account of living in a tent as a child. CBS News reported that the spot appeared to insinuate that Acton had mental health issues.

The ad became one of the most controversial moments of the campaign and drew criticism from members of Ramaswamy’s own party.

Acton’s childhood and court records

Amy Acton has spoken publicly for years regarding her difficult childhood and past family background in Ohio. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM / MEGA

Acton has spoken publicly about her difficult childhood for years.

According to police and court records obtained by the Associated Press, Donna Arthur lost custody of her children after her husband, Cledith Arthur, was arrested and charged with raping Acton when she was 12.

The alleged abuse occurred between December 1976 and April 1978. Cledith failed to appear for a court date and became a fugitive. Donna Arthur remained married to him until his death in 2004.

Acton has said she has not seen her mother since 1978.

Acton’s brother, Philip Stearns, said in a statement released by the her campaign that their mother lost custody after Cledith’s arrest and the charges against him. Stearns said the couple remained together until Cledith’s death.

Republicans criticize the ad

The advertisement drew criticism from several Republicans, including Ohio Governor Mike DeWine.

DeWine told reporters that he believed running the ad was “wrong” and said it should have been removed.

Political commentator Meghan McCain also criticized the advertisement, calling it “dastardly” on social media.

Donald Trump and Vice President J.D. Vance defended the spot.

“It’s a mother speaking badly against Amy Acton, and to me, it’s very easy,” Trump told reporters. “If it were my mother speaking badly about me, you’d be making it the number one story in the news.”

The controversy did not appear to help Ramaswamy’s campaign as Acton went on to win the election.

Acton makes Ohio history

The Associated Press called the race for Acton on election night, making her the first woman elected governor of Ohio.

She also became the first Democrat to win an Ohio gubernatorial election since 2006.

With 98 percent of the vote counted, Acton led Ramaswamy 52.3 percent to 44.4 percent, a margin of 7.93 percentage points.

The result was notable because Ohio voted for Trump by 11 points in 2024.

Democrats also scored other Ohio wins

Acton was not the only Democrat to win statewide.

Former Senator Sherrod Brown defeated Republican Senator Jon Husted in the Senate race. Democrats also flipped three Republican-held House seats:

  • Brian Poindexter defeated Rep. Max Miller in the 7th District.
  • Kristina Knickerbocker defeated Rep. Mike Turner in the 10th District.
  • Don Leonard defeated Rep. Mike Carey in the 15th District.

Democrat Allison Russo also won the secretary of state race.

The results gave Democrats a broader victory in a state that has increasingly leaned Republican in recent presidential elections.

Acton’s political background

Acton previously led the Ohio Department of Health during the COVID-19 pandemic and directed a childhood vaccination initiative in the state.

She served in DeWine’s administration before resigning in June 2020 and had never previously held elected office.

During her campaign, Acton positioned herself toward the political center. She supported a ballot measure that would add Ohio’s photo ID requirement to the state constitution.

She also told The Toledo Blade that she does “not support boys playing in girls sports,” a position that drew criticism from some progressives.

On November 4, Acton described her victory as “just the beginning” in a post on X.

“Now, we get to work building an Ohio where every family has the chance to do more than just get by — they can get ahead. That starts with lowering costs, creating opportunity, and making sure every Ohioan has the chance to build a great life. A new day for Ohio starts now,” she wrote.

Acton’s refusal to engage with Ramaswamy marks an early indication of how sharply the campaign’s most contentious moments could shape the relationship between Ohio’s incoming Democratic governor and the Republican political establishment.

title: Democrat Gina Hinojosa appoints a Republican former lawmaker to her transition leadership team in her first official move as governor-elect of Texas: ‘People are tired of the divisions, of the fighting’
content:
Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, a Democrat, has appointed former Republican state Representative Ernest Bailes to her transition leadership team as she prepares to take office in January 2027.

Bailes, a conservative from East Texas, is among the first four people selected to help shape Hinojosa’s incoming administration. The appointment reflects her pledge to govern across party lines after defeating three-term Republican Governor Greg Abbott in the November 3 election.

At a news conference in Austin on November 5, Hinojosa said she deliberately chose a bipartisan team to help deliver on her campaign promises.

“People are tired of the divisions, of the fighting,” she said.

“This is a time to come together in a way that is about just delivering for the people of Texas,” Hinojosa added.

Hinojosa pledges bipartisan government

Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa appointed Republican Ernest Bailes to her transition leadership team before taking office. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM / MEGA

The announcement was Hinojosa’s first public appearance since defeating Abbott. She said her administration would represent Texans across the political spectrum, rather than only the Democrats who supported her campaign.

“I am not going to be the governor for just Democrats. I am going to be the governor for all the people of Texas,” Hinojosa said.

“We will have a bipartisan transition, and we will have a bipartisan administration and government in Texas,” she added.

Bailes served in the Texas House from 2017 to 2025. He will co-chair the transition team with Ryan Pollock, executive director of the Texas State Building and Construction Trades Council.

Who is Ernest Bailes?

Gina Hinojosa praised Bailes’ work on public education, calling him a close ally despite their party differences. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM / MEGA

Bailes is a fifth-generation East Texan, rancher and businessman from Shepherd and a Texas A&M graduate. At the Austin news conference, he introduced himself as a “conservative Republican,” according to The Texas Tribune.

Hinojosa highlighted Bailes’ work on public education and described him as a close ally despite their party differences.

“In fact, I count him as one of my best allies for public schools. That is his commitment. There is really little light between our positions on public education,” she said.

Voucher fight brought Bailes and Hinojosa closer

Bailes’ opposition to Greg Abbott’s private school voucher proposal put him at direct odds with the former governor. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM / MEGA

Bailes’ opposition to Abbott’s private school voucher proposal was one of the issues that put him at odds with the governor.

In 2023, Bailes joined Democrats and other Republicans in opposing Abbott’s proposal to use public money to help families pay for private education.

Abbott responded by backing primary challengers against Republican lawmakers who opposed his voucher plan. In 2024, Janis Holt won the Republican primary for Texas House District 18 with Abbott’s endorsement, defeating Bailes by about 4,000 votes.

Despite their different party affiliations, Bailes said he was ready to work with Hinojosa.

“We will work together for what is best for the kids of the state of Texas. We will be able to take care of education, and we will support and listen to the people,” he said.

The San Antonio Current also reported Bailes saying, “We will put partisanship aside.”

Who else is joining the transition team?

Hinojosa announced three other appointments alongside Bailes and Pollock.

Joe Madden, a Houston public affairs consultant who previously worked in the Texas Legislature and Harris County government, will serve as executive director. Axios reported that Madden is a former chief of staff to Harris County Judge Lina Hidalgo and has experience in state government and emergency management.

Tamala Barksdale, a former Austin Independent School District trustee who served alongside Hinojosa on the school board, will serve as a senior adviser.

Ryan Pollock, executive director of the Texas State Building and Construction Trades Council, will co-chair the transition team with Bailes.

The appointments reflect several priorities from Hinojosa’s campaign, particularly public education and organized labor.

Hinojosa pledged to increase public school funding and replace Texas Education Agency Commissioner Mike Morath with an educator. Pollock’s appointment also reflects her focus on creating well-paid jobs and supporting working Texans.

Hinojosa begins search for education commissioner

Hinojosa said her team is already “actively interviewing people” to replace Morath, who has led the Texas Education Agency since January 2016.

Morath’s current appointment expires January 10, 2027, nine days before Hinojosa takes office. That timing could allow Hinojosa to appoint a successor rather than formally remove him.

Her nominee would still need confirmation from the Republican-controlled Texas Senate.

Hinojosa’s historic election

Hinojosa defeated Abbott in the November 3 general election, becoming the first Latina elected governor of Texas and the first Democrat to win the office in more than three decades.

Preliminary Associated Press results showed Hinojosa with 52.8 percent of the vote to Abbott’s 45.7 percent. The figures remained unofficial pending certification.

Abbott conceded on election night.

“Mathematically, we’re not going to be able to win this election,” he said.

What comes next

Gina Hinojosa’s transition team will expand as staff reviews applications prior to her Jan. 19, 2027, inauguration. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM / MEGA

Hinojosa’s transition team is expected to grow as her staff reviews applications and makes additional appointments ahead of her January 19, 2027, inauguration.

The transition operation has launched a website and online résumé portal for Texans interested in serving in the incoming administration. The effort is operating under the name “By and For the People.”

Bailes’ appointment gives Hinojosa an early bipartisan voice on her transition team while signaling that public education will be a major priority of her incoming administration.

title: Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis warns ‘the Senate should pull all-nighters for as long as it takes’ to confirm President Donald Trump’s remaining federal judicial nominees as he becomes a lame duck
content:
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis is urging Senate Republicans to work around the clock to confirm President Donald Trump‘s remaining judicial nominees before Democrats take control of the chamber in January.

“Every single federal judicial vacancy needs to be filled in the lame duck session,” DeSantis wrote on X on November 6, 2026. He added that senators “should pull all-nighters for as long as it takes.”

“Democrats [won’t] confirm a single Trump judge once they take over,” DeSantis wrote.

His warning came three days after the November 3 midterm elections, in which Democrats won control of the Senate.

What DeSantis wants Republicans to do

The Hill reported on November 7 that DeSantis made the remarks on social media. In a separate interview with Fox News host Laura Ingraham, he argued that Republicans should treat the remaining weeks as an emergency.

Asked what Republicans should do with their remaining time in control of the Senate, DeSantis said he would “roll in cots” to the Senate cloakroom and keep senators working around the clock.

He argued that Republicans would not be able to confirm conservative judges once Democrats take control on January 3 for the remainder of Trump’s term, according to the interview report.

DeSantis also previously warned that Trump would have virtually no chance of replacing Supreme Court Justices Clarence Thomas or Samuel Alito during his presidency if either justice retires.

He described the chance as “zero” and said the odds of a replacement under a Republican administration from 2029 to 2033 were “probably zero.”

Democrats’ Senate victory

Democrats are projected to win at least 54 Senate seats, including victories in traditionally Republican states such as Texas, Kansas and South Carolina.

Depending on the results in Alaska and Mississippi, Democrats could enter the new Congress with as many as 56 seats, The Hill reported.

Newsweek reported that Democrats flipped at least seven Senate seats and more than two dozen House seats, although some races remained unresolved several days after the election.

Republicans will retain control of the Senate until the 120th Congress is sworn in on January 3, 2027.

That leaves Republicans with a narrow window to act on Trump’s judicial nominees.

White House backs confirmation push

The White House said it expects Trump’s pending judicial nominees to be confirmed before the current Congress ends.

“We expect all judicial nominees pending in the Senate to be confirmed this year,” a White House official said on November 6.

The current Congress has confirmed 57 judges since Trump began his second term in 2025.

The administration’s remaining vacancies and judicial nominees are harder to count because different sources use different definitions and dates.

One tally cited by The Hill, based on Federal Judicial Center data, counted 28 federal judicial vacancies, including 11 with nominees pending. That would leave additional nominees awaiting Senate action for future vacancies.

Mike Davis, president of the Article III Project, wrote in a November 7 Fox News column that 23 judicial nominees remained pending.

Law professor JP Collins reached the same figure in a November 9 analysis for Balls and Strikes.

Three nominees are ready for floor votes

Three Trump nominees appear particularly well-positioned for confirmation because they have already cleared the Senate Judiciary Committee:

  • Anna St. John: Nominated in July for the Fifth Circuit seat being vacated by retiring Judge Kurt Engelhardt, St. John cleared the Judiciary Committee on September 24 and is awaiting a full Senate vote.
  • Daniel Desmond Domenico: Nominated for the Tenth Circuit seat of retiring Judge Timothy Tymkovich, Domenico’s nomination reached the Senate in May and cleared committee in July.
  • Gregory Carl Cook: Nominated for the Northern District of Alabama to replace retiring Judge R. David Proctor, Cook’s nomination was received by the Senate in July and cleared committee in September.

A tight Senate schedule

The Senate returned to Washington on November 9, leaving Republicans with a crowded legislative calendar.

The tentative schedule includes a Thanksgiving recess from November 23 through November 27 and a target adjournment date of December 18.

Collins calculated that the Senate is scheduled to meet for only 30 days during the remainder of the year. Those days include November 9 and 10, the week of November 16 and the three weeks from November 30 through December 18.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune, a South Dakota Republican, said in September that judicial nominees were among the chamber’s priorities.

He described the remaining period as a “big but limited opportunity.”

Other Republicans push for action

DeSantis is not the only Republican demanding faster action on Trump’s nominees.

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier urged the Senate to confirm district court nominee Robert Long, calling him one of the “finest jurists” and criticizing the Senate for leaving his nomination pending for months.

Mike Davis has also pressed Republican senators to move more quickly.

Davis urged Arkansas Sens. Tom Cotton and John Boozman to confirm Lee Rudofsky to an appeals court seat. He wrote on X that the senators “wanted someone else” and needed to change course “fast.”

Spokespeople for Cotton and Boozman did not respond to requests for comment.

Supreme Court vacancies add urgency

The push to confirm lower-court judges comes amid renewed speculation about potential Supreme Court retirements.

Thomas is 78 and Alito is 76. Neither has indicated that he plans to leave the Court soon.

Alito told CBS News in an interview that aired in October that he had “thought about” stepping down but decided he could still contribute.

After the election, The New York Times and Bloomberg reported that Alito had again told people he did not intend to retire immediately.

Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer of New York indicated that Democrats would resist adding another conservative justice.

“We’re not going to allow a right-winger on the court,” Schumer told The Associated Press.

DeSantis prepares to leave office

DeSantis is term-limited and will leave the Florida governor’s office in January 2027.

At a post-election news conference in Tallahassee, he said Republicans nationally were in a “deep hole” while arguing that Florida had held the line.

Of his remaining time in office, DeSantis said there was “more work to do until the lights are out.”

The governor’s push for judicial confirmations comes as he prepares to leave office and remains one of the Republican Party’s prominent figures ahead of the 2028 presidential cycle.

Federal district and appeals court judges are nominated by the president, confirmed by the Senate and serve for life. Nominees must first clear the Senate Judiciary Committee, while full Senate confirmation requires a simple majority.

title: Pentagon spokesperson says Pete Hegseth’s wife is ‘in full compliance with all ethics laws,’ calls concerns about her work with a consulting firm with alleged links to a military supplier ‘ridiculous slander’
content:
The Pentagon has defended Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and his wife, Jennifer Hegseth, after questions emerged over her consulting work for a Washington firm that has had defense contractor Lockheed Martin as a client.

Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said that both Hegseths are “in full compliance with all ethics laws and regulations” and dismissed suggestions of a conflict of interest as “ridiculous slander.”

There is no evidence that Jennifer worked directly with Lockheed Martin, advised the company on defense matters or influenced Pentagon decisions.

Pentagon says Hegseths followed ethics rules

The Pentagon defended Pete and Jennifer Hegseth following ethics questions regarding her consulting firm’s defense ties. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM/MEGA

Parnell said that “any insinuations or claims otherwise are ridiculous slander.”

He said the Department of Defense maintains a “rigorous, multilayered ethics framework” that includes financial disclosure reviews, divestitures when necessary and screening procedures designed to prevent conflicts of interest.

The Pentagon spokesperson said that “robust administrative firewalls” are also established and enforced when required. According to Parnell, those measures ensure senior officials are “completely screened from matters involving former employers or private interests.”

A spokesperson for Watchtower Strategy, the firm where she is listed as a consultant, told Newsweek that she “has not interfaced with any clients nor does she provide any advice to Watchtower on defense matters.”

Why Jennifer’s work raised questions

Pete Hegseth’s financial disclosure lists his wife as a consultant to Watchtower Strategy, a D.C. firm co-founded by Kevin McCarthy. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM/MEGA

Pete’s annual financial disclosure lists his wife as a consultant to Watchtower Strategy, a Washington public relations and advocacy firm.

The company was co-founded in early 2025 by former House Speaker Kevin McCarthy. Politico reported on November 4 that Watchtower was founded in January 2025 and that Lockheed Martin was among its clients that year.

The disclosure does not specify how much Jennifer was paid or whether she continues to work with the firm.

A Watchtower spokesperson said she assisted the company with “navigating conservative TV media.”

The spokesperson did not say whether that work is ongoing.

The available information does not establish that Jennifer had any direct relationship with Lockheed Martin or performed work for the defense contractor.

Hegseth faces political pressure

The questions about the consulting work emerged as Pete faced growing political pressure over the war with Iran and Republican losses in the November 3 midterm elections.

President Donald Trump said on November 5 that he had “every intention” of keeping Hegseth as defense secretary.

Hegseth also pushed back against the criticism in a video message that day, saying he would “not back down.”

Jennifer, a longtime former Fox News producer, has remained a visible presence alongside her husband.

In August, she was named chair of Trump’s Military Spouse Commission, a voluntary advisory position.

Her late father reportedly worked as an executive at Lockheed Martin, adding another point of interest to questions surrounding her professional and family connections to the defense industry.

However, the Pentagon and Watchtower have denied any suggestion that her consulting role created an ethics violation or gave her influence over Defense Department decisions.

title: Wisconsin infant dies after contracting measles, becomes first person in the state to die of the disease in nearly four decades
content:
An infant in southwestern Wisconsin has died after contracting measles, marking the state’s first death from the disease in 36 years, state health officials announced Thursday.

The death is the first measles-related death reported in Wisconsin since 1990 and comes as the state faces its largest measles outbreak in more than three decades.

What Wisconsin officials said

The Wisconsin Department of Health Services confirmed that the coroner determined measles as the immediate cause of death. By: CDC/UNSPLASH

The Wisconsin Department of Health Services said the coroner determined that measles was the immediate cause of death.

DHS Secretary Kirsten Johnson addressed the death in a statement.

“It is with a heavy heart we are reporting the first death of an infant connected with a measles outbreak in Wisconsin in many years,” Johnson said. “My heart is broken for the family.”

Johnson added that the death of any child is a tragedy, particularly when it involves a vaccine-preventable disease.

DHS did not disclose where the infant died or provide additional details, citing the family’s privacy.

Measles outbreak continues to grow

DHS confirmed the infant death was directly associated with an ongoing and expanding measles outbreak in southern Wisconsin. By: CDC/UNSPLASH

DHS said the death was associated with an ongoing measles outbreak in southern Wisconsin.

The state has reported 431 measles cases across 13 counties in 2026, the highest total in more than 35 years. Nine people have been hospitalized.

The outbreak has expanded steadily in recent months.

The outbreak in Grant, Iowa and Lafayette counties had produced 151 confirmed and six probable cases. DHS had confirmed 267 measles cases statewide, with the outbreak reaching Vernon County.

Wisconsin health officials had declared an outbreak in Lafayette and Iowa counties shortly before the fall school year began.

Dr. Ryan Westergaard, Wisconsin’s chief medical officer, told CNN that measles continues to spread because enough people remain susceptible to allow the virus to find new hosts.

Health officials say about 95 percent of the population needs to be vaccinated to maintain protection against measles. Two doses of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine are about 97 percent effective.

Other measles deaths reported nationwide

The Wisconsin death came days after two other measles-associated deaths were reported in the United States.

A child in New York’s Lewis County died Sunday, November 1, in the state’s first known measles-associated death in more than 30 years. State and local officials said the child was unvaccinated and died at the family’s home.

Pennsylvania reported another measles-associated death.

The person was an unvaccinated resident of Jefferson County. Funeral director Brenda Shumaker identified the person as a 21-year-old woman who suffered complications after giving birth at home.

CDC death count differs from state reports

There is a discrepancy between the number of measles deaths reported by states and the count published by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

The Washington Post reported that the CDC updated its website on November 4 to list four measles deaths in 2026.

Pennsylvania has reported six measles-associated deaths, while New York has reported one and Wisconsin has now reported one.

The CDC said it is working with state epidemiologists to establish a standardized definition for reporting measles deaths. The agency counts deaths that are confirmed and reported directly to it.

U.S. measles cases reach highest level since 1991

The CDC reports 5,182 measles cases in the United States in 2026, the highest annual total since 1991.

Pennsylvania is experiencing the country’s largest outbreak. As of November 4, the state had recorded 1,467 cases across 45 counties.

The national outbreak has also raised questions about the United States’ measles elimination status.

The Pan American Health Organization is scheduled to meet from November 10 to 13 to determine whether the United States will retain its measles elimination status. The country has held that designation since 2000.

No decision had been announced at the time of writing.

The Wisconsin infant’s death underscores the continuing impact of the nationwide measles resurgence as health officials work to contain outbreaks and prevent further deaths.

title: Attorney General Todd Blanche floats DOJ investigation after President Donald Trump accused Democratic lawmakers of ‘extortion at the highest level’ for threatening Republicans with impeachment
content:
Attorney General Todd Blanche left open the possibility that Democratic lawmakers could face a Department of Justice investigation after President Donald Trump ordered the department to examine what he described as threats, extortion and “lawfare” against administration officials, Republican donors and supporters.

Blanche did not announce an investigation or identify a federal criminal statute that Democratic lawmakers were suspected of violating.

What Blanche said on CNN

Todd Blanche left open the possibility that Democratic lawmakers could face DOJ investigations following Donald Trump’s directive. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM / MEGA

Appearing on CNN’s State of the Union, Blanche argued that some recent Democratic rhetoric went beyond legitimate congressional oversight. He declined to identify specific criminal conduct when host Dana Bash pressed him.

“You have free speech in this country,” Blanche said. “You are allowed to be critical of President Trump, of me, of this administration. But when the threats become so vile and so dangerous…at some point you have to draw the line.”

Bash then asked whether the DOJ would investigate lawmakers and whether the conduct described constituted a crime.

“It depends on what’s said. So yes, it could be,” Blanche replied. “I’m not saying that necessarily every case is going to be prosecuted.”

Asked about Trump’s characterization of Democrats as “extortionists” who belong in prison, Blanche said the answer depended on what laws had allegedly been broken.

“Well, it depends on what the crime is and what they’ve done,” he said.

Blanche said Trump was responding to Democratic rhetoric after the midterm elections.

“That is not government. That is not leading. That is not oversight,” he said.

Trump orders DOJ to investigate

Donald Trump demanded a DOJ investigation into Democrats in a Truth Social post. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM/MEGA

Trump made the demand in a Truth Social post on November 7, 2026.

He accused Democrats of threatening Blanche and other officials with impeachment and “many other forms of punishment.” He also alleged that Democratic lawmakers were targeting Republican donors “with imprisonment and many other levels of punishment, just because they happen to be Republicans, or Republican supporters.”

“This is extortion at the highest level and they should be held accountable for this,” Trump wrote. “This is Weaponization and Lawfare at another level.”

He added: “The imprisonment should be against these EXTORTIONISTS…By copy of this statement, I am ordering the Department of Justice to look into this criminal act, immediately!”

Slotkin responds to Trump

Donald Trump’s Truth Social post focused in part on Michigan Democratic Sen. Elissa Slotkin’s comments about administrative hiring. By: ZUMAPRESS.COM/MEGA

Trump’s post focused in part on Senator Elissa Slotkin, a Michigan Democrat.

Slotkin had discussed the possibility of future legal scrutiny discouraging people from joining the Trump administration during an October 13 event at the University of Chicago.

“I want young people coming out of school to say, ‘Should I go work for the Trump administration? … Lord, that might be buying myself a ton of problems that I don’t want and so let me avoid participating in that,’” Slotkin said. “I want that deterrence message.”

Slotkin rejected Trump’s accusations in a statement posted on X and emailed to Newsweek on November 7.

She said accountability should be based on whether someone broke the law rather than their political affiliation.

“If you break the law or use taxpayer dollars to enrich yourself, you should be held accountable,” Slotkin said. “If you didn’t break the law, then it’s all good.”

Blanche warns over Democratic oversight

Blanche also pointed to comments from incoming House Oversight Committee Chairman Robert Garcia, a California Democrat.

Garcia has promised an “aggressive” series of investigations into the Trump administration and the president’s family. He also warned incoming White House chief of staff Stephen Miller to “lawyer up.”

Blanche acknowledged that Congress has a constitutional role to conduct oversight.

“I welcome oversight. Oversight is exactly something they should be doing,” he said.

But he warned that the Justice Department would intervene if congressional investigations became what he described as improper targeting of White House officials.

“If they try to come after Stephen Miller for these whatever it is that Garcia thinks he’s going to do, instead of actually just conducting oversight and leading, of course the Department of Justice will be there to defend him,” Blanche said.

Raskin raises impeachment possibility

Rep. Jamie Raskin of Maryland, a Democrat who could chair the House Judiciary Committee in the next Congress, said Blanche himself could face impeachment hearings.

Speaking to MS NOW, Raskin cited Blanche’s handling of the Jeffrey Epstein case and what he described as the DOJ’s pursuit of Trump’s political opponents.

“The Department of Justice has clearly become a Department of Injustice — an instrument of revenge, political revenge for the president,” Raskin said. “… This attorney general has been doing nothing other than acting in his old capacity as a personal criminal defense attorney to Donald Trump.”

Divided government sets up new clash

The exchange points to a growing confrontation between the Trump administration and congressional Democrats after the November 3 midterm elections.

Democrats won control of both the House and Senate, giving them subpoena power and the ability to launch investigations into the administration when the new Congress begins in January 2027.

The shift creates divided government for the final two years of Trump’s term and sets up potential clashes over congressional oversight, executive power and the Justice Department.

title: John Mulaney Blasts Robert F. Kennedy Jr. on 'SNL': 'Dumbass'
content:
John Mulaney tore into Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. on Saturday Night Live, branding him a “dumbass.”

“No one likes that guy anymore,” Mulaney, 44, quipped during his Saturday, November 14, standup comedy monologue. “What a predicament to be in. I have right-wing friends who used to be into him. Now, no one likes him.”

He added, “You dumbass! Your thing can’t be the measles. That can’t be your project! Giving people the measles and hoping they [live].”

(Measles cases have reportedly risen to a 35-year high under Kennedy’s tenure as HHS secretary, with the Centers for Disease Control confirming 5,412 cases across 47 different regions this year.)

Rosie O'Donnell Accuses RFK Jr. of 'Defiling' His Family's Legacy

Mulaney repeatedly referred to Kennedy, 72, as “Bobby” throughout his monologue, revealing that he’s “known that dude for more than a decade.”

“You shouldn’t be in the government if I’ve known you for over a decade,” he joked. “I know some whack-ass people!”

The comedian recalled that he was introduced to Kennedy back when the future HHS secretary was working as an environmental lawyer. (Kennedy received a Juris Doctor law degree from the University of Virginia School of Law in 1982 and later earned a master’s degree in environmental law from the Pace University School of Law in 1987.)

“He wasn’t really [a lawyer]. He would just join cases late if they were about to be successful,” Mulaney alleged. “He had this stupid organization in New York, they were called the Riverkeepers.”

Kennedy has been associated with environmental action in the Hudson River since the 1980s, having formed the Riverkeepers organization to help keep its tributaries clean. (The New York City Department of Environmental Protection has determined that the Hudson River is safe to swim in, though there have been numerous allegations of contamination in the past.)

“They were in charge of keeping the Hudson River in New York City clean,” Mulaney said. “That was his job. That’s how good he is at jobs. His old job was keeping the Hudson River — whose native fish was tied-off used condom — clean. Now, he’s in charge of all of our tummies.”

Mulaney closed his monologue by comparing Kennedy’s gravely voice to “the mom from Goonies.” (Kennedy’s strained and shaky voice is caused by a neurological condition known as spasmodic dysphonia.)

Us has reached out to the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services for comment.

Saturday’s monologue was far from the first time Mulaney has publicly mocked Kennedy. During his Netflix “Night of Too Many Stars” comedy set in May, he accused Kennedy of cheating on his wife, Cheryl Hines, “like a dog.”

“Sorry for the pearl clutch,” he quipped. “There are some West Side people who know exactly what I’m talking about. Sorry to drop that public domain information on the Hollywood Bowl.”

Mulaney was seemingly referring to allegations that Kennedy was sexting New York Magazine reporter Olivia Nuzzi while she covered his 2024 presidential campaign. The publication claimed that Nuzzi, 33, had not disclosed her “personal relationship” with a candidate she was covering, though its statement stopped short of directly naming Kennedy. (Nuzzi and New York Magazine eventually parted ways, though the publication found “no inaccuracies nor evidence of bias” in her coverage.)

“The relationship was never physical but should have been disclosed to prevent the appearance of a conflict,” Nuzzi told The New York Times at the time. “I deeply regret not doing so immediately and apologize to those I’ve disappointed, especially my colleagues at New York.”

RFK Jr. never directly responded to the allegations, only telling Fox News in September 2024 that he “never comment[s] on those kinds of stories.” Hines seemingly downplayed the rumors about Nuzzi in September 2025, telling the “Katie Miller Podcast” that people should “consider the source.”

“I don’t know this person. Don’t know their intentions. I could guess, but I won’t,” she said of Nuzzi.

title: Brandi Glanville Reveals She Had 'Black Mass' Removed During Facial Surgery
content:
Brandi Glanville is sharing the shocking news that she had a “black mass” removed when she recently underwent an exploratory facial surgery.

“They did find some things that they sent away for pathology,” Glanville, 53, announced on the Friday, November 13, episode of her “Brandi Glanville Unfiltered” podcast. “That’s not back yet. However, I have so much fluid in my head it’s crazy.”

During Friday’s podcast, Glanville mentioned that doctors “don’t know yet” what the “black mass” actually is.

“[The doctor] said there were several of them,” she said. “He only took one out. I’m not sure what that is yet. My recovery hasn’t been painful.”

Brandi Glanville Shares Health Update After Facial Disfigurement

The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills alum confirmed in October that she’d scheduled a facial surgery with Dr. Carlo Henrado in hopes of getting to the bottom of health issues that have plagued her for more than three years.

Glanville initially thought she had a facial parasite in 2023 but was told earlier this year that she may actually be suffering from “highly resistant ESBL Klebsiella and Enterobacter with biofilm, Coccidioidomycosis (Valley Fever), Demodex dermatitis and Mononucleosis.” (The reality star estimated in April 2025 that she’d spent more than $113,000 on treatment options.)

“We are excited because we did get a few answers,” she shared during a post-op podcast this week. “There’s an infection in my glands that is … antibiotic resistant.”

Glanville confirmed she is on “antibiotics almost 24 hours a day” and is starting to “see a difference.”

“I’m excited about that,” she beamed. “I just can’t wait to go back outside and be normal. It’s coming, guys!”

Before going under the knife, Glanville claimed on her podcast that her doctor was going to “take my face off” and “do a power wash under my skin.”

Brandi Glanville Praises Yolanda Hadid’s Support Amid Health Battle

“[The doctor] is, like, literally going in there with a power washer, basically, and knives and all this s***,” she explained. “And then he’s spinning my blood and doing this platelet thing on the inside of my face. We might not want my blood at this point.”

One of Brandi’s friends launched a GoFundMe in September to help her pay for ongoing medical expenses. Kyle Richards, Camille Grammer and Vicki Gunvalson were among the Bravolebrities who donated, helping to push the fundraising appeal to more than $23,600 as of publication.

“I’m honestly overwhelmed by all the love and support,” Brandi wrote via September 12 Instagram Story. “Thank you to every single person who has donated, shared my GoFundMe, checked on me, prayed for me or sent me love.”

In the middle of her latest health crisis, Brandi announced on October 10 that her dad, Guy Glanville, died at age 77.

“I feel guilty sometimes for being happy on certain days,” Glanville admitted on Friday’s podcast. “I often talk to [lost loved ones above] and I know they’re in a better place. This is the hardest time of my life.”

title: Journey Drummer Deen Castronovo Exits Band Mid-Tour Due to 'Health Matters'
content:
Journey is pushing ahead with its Final Frontier Tour following the departure of the band’s longtime drummer, Deen Castronovo.

“After careful consideration and an extensive year of touring, our talented, longtime drummer Deen Castronovo has decided to step away to focus on personal health matters that require his attention,” the “Open Arms” band revealed via a Friday, November 13, statement. “He has our full support during this time and extends his heartfelt thanks to the fans for the love, encouragement, and kindness he has received.”

The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductees have enlisted fill-in drummer Steve Murphy for the remainder of this year’s dates on Journey’s farewell tour.

“Native New Yorker Steve Murphy who comes to us from working with bands such as Alan Parsons Project, Trans Siberian Orchestra, Christopher Cross and Jack Bruce will be joining us for the remainder of November,” the band confirmed via Instagram. “We look forward to continuing to share unforgettable nights of music with all of you.”

Jon Bon Jovi Abruptly Ends NYC Concert Early: 'I'm Gonna Have to Cool It'

Castronovo’s shocking departure from Journey follows two recent incidents where he had to exit the stage mid-performance, forcing his bandmates to rearrange their show on the fly, with drum tech Steve Toomey ultimately filling in on both occasions.

Viral footage captured Journey announcing from the stage at the BOK Center in Tulsa on October 8 that Castronovo was being rushed to the hospital due to a “medical emergency” after performing only 2 songs in a planned 28-song setlist.

“We’re going to see what happens as this progresses,” Journey keyboardist and rhythm guitarist Jonathan Cain explained to fans that night. “It’s an unfortunate situation. We’re very sorry. We’re hoping it’s only a delay, but please — I’m sorry. Don’t worry. Have your prayers ready. Have your prayers ready for Deen Castronovo, everybody. Thank you.”

Journey frontman Arnel Pineda assured fans after an extended break that the drummer was “going to be fine.” Later in the show, lead guitarist Neal Schon dedicated the rest of the Tulsa show to Castronovo.

“This concert’s for Deen tonight,” he told the audience. “I’d love you all to pray for him. Everybody’s been going through a lot. I think he’s going to be fine.”

Castronovo was back on stage with Journey on October 10 at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, though he was again rushed from the stage in Boston after performing 12 songs on Tuesday, November 10.

REO Speedwagon Retires From Touring Due to ‘Irreconcilable Differences’

Journey has not disclosed exactly what medical issues Castronovo is dealing with.

Prior to joining Journey in 1998, Castronovo played with singer John Waite and future Journey bandmates Schon, 72, and Cain, 76, in rock supergroup Bad English from 1987 to 1991. He later joined Ozzy Osbourne‘s backing band in 1995.

Journey’s Final Frontier Tour is set to wrap up for the year at the Honda Center in Anaheim on November 24.

title: 'Chicago Fire' Actress Robyn Coffin Announces Breast Cancer Diagnosis
content:
Chicago Fire actress Robyn Coffin is expected to undergo surgery after being diagnosed with breast cancer.

“Robyn has been diagnosed with breast cancer. Terrible news,” a statement on her GoFundMe page read. “The good news – she has a crack team at the hospital organizing and planning her surgery and aftercare and recovery.”

Coffin set up the fundraising page with friend Gianine DeFrancesco in hopes of supporting the actress through her upcoming operation and recovery. An initial fundraising goal has been set at $75,000, with more than $15,000 already raised as of publication.

“When Robyn doesn’t work, she doesn’t get paid,” DeFrancesco clarfied via GoFundMe. “So, this go fund me is not only to fill in the gaps that insurance will surely leave, but also to help sustain Robyn and [her husband] Grant while Robyn is off work. Thank goodness they have insurance, but let’s not get cocky – let’s give them a nest egg because we know there will be surprises.”

Baywatch’s Nicole Eggert Says More Cancer Was Found in Lymph Nodes

Coffin is expected to have a right partial mastectomy with magseed localization on December 3, followed by a course of radiation. First, she will meet with her care team on November 24 to make a final decision on whether a partial or full mastectomy will be the best treatment option.

“If that visit results in affirming the right partial mastectomy, Robyn is expecting to be out of work for 3 weeks,” DeFrancesco explained. “If a full mastectomy is required, Robyn’s time off work will increase quite a bit, as the surgery is much more extensive.”

Fans were assured in the fundraising appeal that Coffin will be able to count on her “husband Grant and supportive friends [as] wonderful caregivers.”

“We know that with insurance the surgery and hospital bill will amount to $40k. Because the surgery is hard upon, this amount is most urgent. The balance is for said surprises: a longer recovery period (see not working), medicine off the plan or not fully covered, or whatever is thrown at them,” DeFrancesco noted. “So, Village – thank you in advance for embracing Robyn with love and support. We’ve got her!”

Coffin’s Chicago Fire costar Miranda Rae Mayo shared a link via Instagram to the GoFundMe page to encourage donations, writing, “This beautiful and wonderful woman is in need of support. You may know her as Cindy Herrmann on our show. Any and everything helps.”

Mayo, 36, and fellow Chicago Fire cast member Hanako Greensmith — who play Stella Kidd and Violet Mikami, respectively — personally donated to help fund Coffin’s treatment.

Coffin is best known for playing Captain Christopher Herrmann‘s (David Eigenberg) wife Cindy Hermann on NBC’s long-running procedural hit Chicago Fire, having recurred or guest starred in each of the show’s 15 seasons. (The character also crossed over to Chicago Med for a 2016 episode.)

Having appeared in more than 60 episodes of Chicago Fire, Cindy’s most memorable story line involved her being diagnosed with lung cancer in season 11. Cindy underwent a grueling regimen of chemotherapy and radiation treatments before being declared cancer-free at the end of the season.

Coffin has also made supporting appearances on many hit shows throughout her career, including Empire and Under Covers.

title: Virgin River's Shocking Exits Over the Years: Biggest Cast Changes
content:
Virgin River has gone through a surprising amount of cast exits through the years.

Based on Robyn Carr’s book series, Virgin River follows the lives of residents living in a small town in Northern California, including Mel (Alexandra Breckenridge) and Jack (Martin Henderson). The hit series, which premiered in 2019, also stars Colin Lawrence, Annette O’Toole, Tim Matheson, Benjamin Hollingsworth, Sarah Dugdale, Zibby Allen and Kai Bradbury.

After seven seasons, there have been some major departures from the Netflix show. Grayson Gurnsey left as Ricky after season 4, and Mark Ghanimé, who played Cameron, had a surprising exit once season 6 was released.

“I think this season saw a little bit of a sendoff for Cameron,” showrunner Patrick Sean Smith exclusively told Us Weekly in December 2024. “In terms of Mark, the actor who I adore, he unfortunately won’t be coming back for season 7.”

Which 'Virgin River' Stars Are — And Aren't — Returning After Cast Exits?

Smith didn’t rule out a potential return for the character in the future. “But that’s not to say that Cameron’s not a part of our world forever,” he added. “I would love to bring him back, and bring his character back when the story presents itself.”

In March 2026, Virgin River returned for season 7, and it was later confirmed that Marco Grazzini will not reprise his role as Mike. In another twist, Lauren Hammersley, who has played Charmaine since the show premiered, is also not expected to come back for season 8.

“For me, I’m just trying to look [at] the longevity of the show and making sure that the characters that we’re keeping have enough story engine in them to keep going,” Smith told Deadline at the time. “So I can’t say there are any specific cast shakeups planned, but I think we will have to start to — as characters run their course — make some decisions and bring in some new blood.”

The show was renewed for season 9 before season 8 premiered on Netflix.

title: Russell Brand's Ex-GF Claims Star Married Katy Perry for 'Fame' in New Doc
content:
Russell Brand‘s ex Jordan Martin has alleged that the disgraced comedian once told her he “always wanted” to marry someone famous before dating his future wife Katy Perry.

“[Russell was] doing exactly what he always wanted to do [with Perry] and be married to someone famous, which he always said he would be,” Martin claimed in the new Netflix documentary Russell Brand: Open Secret.

Martin reportedly dated Brand, 51, for several months in 2007 while he was filming his breakthrough movie, Forgetting Sarah Marshall. In the documentary, Martin recalled that Brand summoned her to the movie’s set in Hawaii because he “wanted someone there to stop him from ‘trying it on’ with people on set,” per Page Six.

“He said to me I should be dating somebody more famous than you,” Martin recalled.

Katy Perry Seemingly Makes Joke About Justin Trudeau Romance

She accused Brand of turning their Hawaiian vacation into a traumatic experience by complaining that she was “dressing like an attention-seeking tart” and insisting he “didn’t feel comfortable” with her sunbathing.

Us has reached out to Brand and Perry’s representatives for comment.

Brand tied the knot with Perry, 42, in India in October 2010. Their marriage proved to be short-lived as he allegedly texted Perry a mere 14 months later in late 2011 to announce he was filing for divorce.

The “Watch It Burn” singer’s raw reaction to Brand’s devastating text message was caught on camera as she was filming her 2012 documentary Katy Perry: Part of Me at the time.

“In the very beginning of me getting into the industry, I would be out and about and I would hear girls, or actresses or musicians or whatever, they would say, ‘Oh no, I don’t want to be in a relationship because I don’t want to have to choose between being in a relationship and having a career,’” Perry explained in Part of Me. “I thought to myself, ‘Pfft, when I find that person that’s going to be my life partner, I will never have to choose because they’ll be accepting of me completely. … They won’t be threatened or have weird motives.’”

She continued, “[My partner] will be accepting of me, the things I love, the ambition, what I aspire to, what I want to create. They’ll be accepting and supportive. I started to realize, ‘Oh my God, that’s not true. That fairytale I had for me is not true for me right now.’”

In another unguarded moment, Perry insisted that she’d done “everything it takes to not fail” in her marriage to Brand.

“[The marriage] still failed,” she lamented. “The bad that comes along with the good is a journey and I learned so much from that journey.”

In a 2013 Vogue interview, Perry alleged that Brand struggled to see her as an “equal” when they were together.

“I felt a lot of responsibility for [the marriage] ending, but then I found out the real truth, which I can’t necessarily disclose because I keep it locked in my safe for a rainy day,” she teased at the time. “I let go and I was like: This isn’t because of me; this is beyond me.’ So I have moved on from that.”

Brand has also spoken publicly about his marriage breakdown over the years, including claiming on his “Stay Free With Russell Brand” podcast in 2025 that Perry was “not entirely normal.”

“She’s an extraordinary, massive star­ — but she’s not weird or off key,” he said at the time. “And wasn’t involved in anything nefarious, as far as I could tell. … The reasons that a marriage didn’t work are the normal human reasons [why] marriages don’t work, and I have nothing but respect for her.”

However, the Get Him to the Greek actor reacted harshly to Perry’s newfound romance with former Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, calling the politician a “globalist stooge.”

“I was OK with Orlando Bloom, but Justin Trudeau? Come on, man! Don’t put me in a category with that guy,” he sniped at a December 2025 Turning Point USA event.

Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison on Monday, November 9, after being convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He is being held in HMP Wandsworth in South London. (The comedian was accused of multiple instances of sexual abuse between 2004 and 2009 by four women.)

Prosecutors Couldn’t Mention Katy Perry in Russell Brand Rape Trial

In the wake of the verdict, London’s Metropolitan Police confirmed to Us that its officers were investigating additional rape allegations made by two unidentified women.

“The suspect has previously been interviewed under caution in connection with the allegations,” a Met spokesperson stated. “Files have been submitted to the Crown Prosecution Service in relation to both complainants.”

Brand has always maintained his innocence and has denied ever having nonconsensual sex.

content:
The late model Presley Gerber‘s 3,000 square-foot Hollywood Hills home is reportedly for sale following his shocking September death at age 27.

Real estate records reportedly indicate that the mid-century dwelling has been listed for $3.595 million, featuring four bedrooms and three baths in addition to outdoor and indoor living spaces, per TMZ.

With an impressive canyon view of the Hollywood Hills, the residence’s reported amenities include a jacuzzi, a cold plunge, a heated pool and a sauna. The property also features a separate guest house.

Gerber reportedly purchased the Los Angeles area home in March 2023 for $3.4 million.

Presley Gerber’s Sober Living Facility Investigated After His Death at Age 27

News broke on September 21 that Presley — son of supermodel Cindy Crawford and Casamigos co-founder Rande Gerber — died one day earlier from a suspected overdose while staying in a Santa Monica rehab center. (The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner confirmed to Us on September 21 that Presley’s cause of death was listed as “deferred” initially because its staff was in the “early stages of investigating” and that “limited information is currently available.”)

The Crawford-Gerber family asked for “privacy during this very difficult and painful time” in a statement obtained by Us on September 21.

Us subsequently learned that officers from the Santa Monica Police Department responded to a call regarding a possible overdose at an address matching the rehab facility on the day of Presley’s death.

“The Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner has identified the individual as Presley Gerber, 27,” a September 21 statement read. “SMPD detectives are investigating the death as a suspected overdose. At this time, there is no indication of foul play. The official cause and manner of death will be determined by the Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner.”

Presley had been open about his struggles with addiction and mental health, including speaking to reporters on a red carpet about his journey of self-acceptance just two months before his untimely death.

“The most free I felt was when I was finally honest with myself,” Presley said at a June We Are ENOUGH x Aviator Nation launch event. “Move your body regardless of how you’re feeling. Get outside. Get some sun. If you don’t feel like moving, lay on the grass.”

During a 2023 “Studio 22” podcast appearance, the Dolce & Gabbana and Ralph Lauren model stated his desire to help people struggling with addiction by sharing his story.

“Whether I help one person or a 100 people get out of that place that I was in at one point in my life, that’s all I need to do,” Presley told podcast listeners at the time. “I’ve had a lot of time to look into myself and learn about myself with therapists. I’ve seen a lot of stuff, and I’ve learned a lot of things, and what I hope I can do is have made the mistakes for some other people so they don’t have to make the same mistakes that I made.”

His parents, Crawford and Randy, 60 and 64 respectively, broke their silence about Presley’s death in October by sharing a new statement reflecting on their son’s life.

“Presley Walker Gerber. July 2, 1999-September 20, 2026. We are beyond heartbroken to lose our beloved son and brother. We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years. He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever,” the couple wrote in a joint statement shared on October 18. “We are so proud of how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability. We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support from so many who know and love our family and even strangers who feel our pain. Til we meet again our sweet boy.”

Inside Kaia Gerber's Relationship With Late Brother Presley Gerber

The same month, Presley’s sister, model and actress Kaia Gerber, penned her own poignant memorial post about the ongoing process of grieving.

“Prez, I don’t have the words, and maybe the tiny mercy is that we didn’t need them all along. Words fail and words subtract and words summarize and words always lack truth. And how naive of me to believe that language could transcend grief,” Kaia, 25, wrote via an October 18 Instagram post. “I’ve read all of the books and I have none of the answers. My articulation is no match against this, the magnitude of losing you. I am, quite literally, down on my f***ing knees.”

The Shards star described her late brother as “inherently good,” adding that she considered herself to be Presley’s “lucky eternal witness” throughout their lives.

“My best buddy, my great protector, the hardest I’ve ever laughed and the one true love of my life — you lit all of my candles and took all of my monsters away. And I love you. And I love you. And I love you. Only you know how much. Thank you for being here,” she concluded.

title: Taylor Frankie Paul Seemingly Applies to Join Bachelor Sam Hartman's Season
content:
Former The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star Taylor Frankie Paul is seemingly shooting her shot with new The Bachelor lead Sam Hartman after her own season of The Bachelorette was postponed indefinitely.

“I chose to have the audacity,” Paul, 32, wrote via Instagram on Friday, November 30, alongside an edited clip featuring Parks and Recreation’s Ron Swanson (Nick Offerman) typing on his computer before unceremoniously throwing the device into a dumpster.

Spliced into the memorable episode was an alleged screenshot of Paul’s application to join the newly-minted Bachelor’s season 30 of the hit reality dating series and in the wake of her own The Bachelorette season’s unprecedented and indefinite pause.

The post featured Paul’s Bachelorette headshot, citing her height as 5’4’’. Under the section, “What do you think would make you stand out amongst the other ladies?” Paul seemingly wrote, “Ahhh I was the first bachelorette in history to be put on hold.”

Taylor Frankie Paul Leaves Flirty Comment About New Bachelor Sam Hartman

The words “ABC going through the submission for the bachelor,” appeared over the edited video showing Offerman’s character throwing out his computer.

After a fan wrote in the comments section of Paul’s post, “Girl get in line like the rest of us,” the reality TV star responded, “As you can see I am. I filled out the paperwork like everyone else.”

Hartman, a quarterback for the Washington Commander’s practice squad, was announced as the new lead of the hit dating franchise on Friday — and like Paul, he is a rather unconventional pick for the beloved series.

“I have a tough time having a conversation with one girl, [so] 30 is gonna be pretty tough,” the professional athlete joked on Good Morning America on Friday after ABC’s surprising announcement. ”I’m excited but also very nervous.”

“Honestly, at first I was like, ‘No way,’” he continued of his reaction to the news he had been selected to lead season 30. “I got really lucky and talked to Jesse Palmer, and he kind of gave me the insight, what it is and what it’s not.”

Paul — whose season 22 of The Bachelorette was shelved indefinitely just three days before its scheduled March premiere after video of her 2023 domestic violence arrest resurfaced — quickly responded to the news Harman would be the next eligible reality TV bachelor.

Taylor Frankie Paul Did ‘Bachelorette’ to Break Free of Toxic Relationship

“Well he’s cute,” Taylor commented under a Friday Instagram announcement regarding Hartman’s casting on The Bachelor.

Earlier this year, leaked video showed Paul hitting and throwing chairs at ex Dakota Mortensen while in the presence of her children. (Paul shares son Ever with Mortensen, 33, and in addition to two older children with her ex-husband, Tate Paul.) She pleaded guilty to aggravated assault in the 2023 case in exchange for the dismissal of additional charges pertaining to child abuse. She completed her three-year probation earlier this year.

“We have made the decision to not move forward with the new season of The Bachelorette at this time, and our focus is on supporting the family,” a Disney Entertainment Television spokesperson told Us in a March 19 statement.
